ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access - UBO declarations are filed with GAFI and the electronic company registry and are accessible to the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit (EFIU), the CBE, and law enforcement; Egypt maintains no public UBO register equivalent to a PSC register regime.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incorporation of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization - Egypt is not a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; therefore documents must pass the full chain: notarization in source state, authentication by source-state Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalization by the Embassy/Consulate of Egypt in the source state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney granted to the Egyptian incorporation agent and authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the country of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (same chain: notary, source-state MFA, then Embassy/Consulate of Egypt)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies of all direct shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) accompanied by source-of-funds declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or competent passport authority of the holder's home state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference / credit standing letter for each non-resident contributing shareholder

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening at formation and continuously thereafter of all shareholders, directors, authorized signatories and UBOs against the OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated lists (1267/1989/2253, 1718, 2231), EU consolidated financial sanctions list, Egypt's CBE terrorist entities and persons list, Interpol red notices, and World Bank debarment list. Any domestic or foreign PEP, family member, or close associate triggers enhanced due diligence with senior compliance officer approval, source-of-wealth/source-of-funds documentation, and ongoing transaction monitoring. The stated payment rails (Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, Stripe) are regulated and commensurate with a low-risk standard AML tier.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) electronic One-Stop-Shop for name clearance and company incorporation (www.gafi.gov.eg; integrated Egypt Business Center portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory corporate name must be in Arabic script and must be distinguishable from existing registered names and trademarks; a Latin-script transliteration may be filed only as a secondary auxiliary designation, while the Arabic name constitutes the legally binding identity. Names must not be misleading, must not breach public order or morality, and must comply with Commercial Law No. 17 of 1999 and GAFI implementing directives.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Arab Republic of Egypt (as leading entity title)
Islamic (without prior Ministry of Endowments clearance)
International / Global / Group (require supporting evidence of substance)
Egyptian / Misr (when misleading as to state sponsorship)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Reserved names may be extended once for an additional 30 days by timely written request before expiry. On rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative protest with the GAFI Name Committee within 30 days of notification, attaching evidence of prior legitimate trading use or trademark registration. If the protest is refused, the applicant may petition the Administrative Court of the Council of State within 60 days of the final administrative decision to annul the rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable as a substitute for a registered head office: Law No. 159 of 1981 requires a physically locatable head office in Egypt for service of process, tax inspection access, and maintenance of corporate records including the UBO register. A genuine serviced or co-working office with dedicated assigned space under a real 12-month lease may be accepted; pure virtual mail-forwarding addresses or letterbox arrangements are rejected by GAFI and expose the entity to non-compliance status and possible strike-off.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate - estimated 20-30% probability of an unannounced GAFI or Egyptian Tax Authority physical inspection within the first 24 months of operation for a low-risk digital content distribution company; risk intensity would rise only if downstream media-specific licensing (e.g., Supreme Council for Media Regulation) is later triggered.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (Articles 1-14, 29-45 for Limited Liabibility Companies), as amended by Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), Commercial Registry Department
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association certified by GAFI and authenticated by the Notary Public
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Egyptian Limited Liability Company under Law No. 72 of 2017; however, the subscribed capital must be fully paid into a temporary bank account opened in the company's name prior to final registration, and bank certificate of deposit must be submitted with the incorporation file.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the subscribers hereby form an Egyptian limited liability company under Law No. 159 of 1981 and Law No. 72 of 2017, with the corporate name and commercial purpose set forth in the Memorandum of Association. That the attached Memorandum and Articles are approved and the registered office is established at the address indicated therein. That the declared initial paid-up capital is subscribed and shall be deposited in a temporary corporate bank account pending irrevocable release to the company treasury. That [Name of Chairman] is appointed Chairman/Manager with sole-signature authority, and [Name of Secretary] is appointed Corporate Secretary responsible for statutory filings. That all directors, officers, and external counsel are authorized to execute all GAFI, Notary, and Commercial Registry filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and Pre-Filing Validation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop / GAFI online investor portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application through the GAFI e-portal or in person at GAFI headquarters; verify the proposed LLC name and commercial purpose code against registered names; obtain the preliminary name approval certificate before preparing the notarial draft.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID copy of each shareholder and manager
Proposed corporate name and three alternates
Notarized power of attorney if filing through a representative
Description of commercial activity including ISIC 5911 digital content production and distribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, immediately file a plural name appeal through GAFI's grievances window, or select an amended distinctive name and re-file; GAFI must issue a formal rejection reason which can be judicially contested before the Economic Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and GAFI Endorsement of the Memorandum of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public General Authority and GAFI One-Stop Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the founders to sign the Arabic Memorandum of Association before the public notary; pay notarization stamp duties; submit the notarized memorandum to GAFI for preliminary endorsement and statutory capital adequacy review.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum of Association
Founders' identification documents
Company name reservation certificate
Lease agreement or letter of intent for registered office premises
Capital subscription schedule signed by founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI queries the memorandum for contractual defects, amend the relevant clause and re-notarize; a supplementary founders' meeting resolution ratifying the amendment suffices to cure the defect without restarting the process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening Temporary Bank Account and Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate bank account using the preliminary GAFI file number and notarized memorandum; deposit the declared paid-up share capital; obtain a certificate of deposit confirming the amount and account details for submission to GAFI.
required_dossiers: Preliminary GAFI incorporation certificate
Notarized Memorandum of Association
Board resolution appointing authorized signatories
Founders' passport copies and tax ID numbers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional beneficial ownership documentation, provide a shareholding registry and declaration of ultimate beneficial owner; if the deposit is rejected due to name mismatch, request GAFI's correction note and re-execute the deposit instruction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Commercial Registry Office and Official Academy of Journalistic Affairs publication department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete statutory package to the GAFI One-Stop Shop; receive the Commercial Registry certificate (shuha ta yo?); complete the mandatory publication of a legal notice in the Egyptian Gazette and conduct the final formalities for the commercial register number.
required_dossiers: GAFI-endorsed Memorandum of Association
Bank certificate of paid-up capital deposit
Registered office lease or ownership title and notarized consent
Copy of preliminary name approval certificate
Signed officers' appointment minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registry delays issuance, submit a written reminder through the GAFI investor services system and escalate to the GAFI grievance committee; missing documents may be supplemented without loss of filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Card, Social Insurance, and Civil Divisions Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Finance Tax Authority, National Organization for Social Insurance, and the General Authority of Civil Defense
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the commercial registry certificate, register for corporate income tax, VAT, and payroll tax; obtain the tax card; register employees with social insurance; file the physical premises safety clearance application.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry certificate
Company constitutional documents and tax ID form
Lease agreement of workplace
Manager national ID and passport copies
Declaration of business activity to tax authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is queried, file an objection within 30 days under Tax Procedures Law; for social insurance discrepancies, submit an amended payroll ledger to the National Organization for Social Insurance.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) - Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B Registration / Limited Environmental Assessment, requiring environmental self-monitoring and site activity registration
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater must comply with Egyptian Ministerial Decree 92/2015 effluent standards (BOD 30 mg/L, COD 100 mg/L, TSS 40 mg/L); VOCs in production studios must be kept below occupational exposure limits consistent with EGS 452/2014; all solid production materials, chemical media waste, and lithium batteries must be stored in closed containers and disposed of through EEAA-approved hazardous and e-waste handlers; air emissions from backup generators must meet MECO air emission limits under Environment Law 4/1994 as amended.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance from the General Administration of Civil Defense of the Ministry of Interior, including fire extinguisher plan, smoke detection system, and emergency evacuation routes; structural load and electrical safety inspection certificate from the competent municipal engineering authority; workplace occupational health clearance from the Ministry of Manpower verifying ventilation, lighting, lighting-level adequacy, and safe wiring for editing and server rooms.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance; electronic services are provided through the ETA eTax portal and the ETA e-invoicing/e-receipt platforms.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An Egyptian LLC must register with the ETA and obtain a tax registration number, generally following incorporation and before commencing taxable activity. The application is submitted through the ETA portal or the competent tax office, supported by the commercial register, articles of association, proof of registered address, authorized representative identification and powers, and other requested corporate records. VAT registration is generally required when taxable turnover reaches the statutory threshold; an application is generally due within 30 days after the registration obligation arises. A nonresident without an Egyptian establishment that supplies electronically delivered services to Egyptian consumers must assess the nonresident simplified VAT-registration rules and register through the ETA’s designated electronic process where applicable. A foreign company operating through an Egyptian permanent establishment or other taxable presence must register under the applicable income-tax and VAT rules. Requirements and portal procedures should be confirmed with the ETA for the particular activity and establishment facts.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt has no US-style check-the-box election for an Egyptian LLC and no general election to treat it as a pass-through entity. An LLC is generally taxed as a separate legal person. No general entity-classification election is available to neutralize hybrid mismatches; applicable treaty, domestic anti-avoidance, and related-party rules must be reviewed.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of taxable sales/turnover during the relevant 12-month period is the general VAT-registration threshold under the VAT Law. Specific activities, including certain professional or service activities, may require registration irrespective of that threshold. Nonresident electronic-service suppliers may be subject to a separate simplified registration regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: ETA e-invoicing requirements apply to in-scope business-to-business transactions under the applicable implementation phases. Invoices must be issued in the prescribed structured electronic format, transmitted to the ETA platform for validation and assigned the required unique identifiers; API integration or approved technical connectivity is required for applicable taxpayers. Electronic receipt requirements apply to in-scope business-to-consumer transactions under the relevant rollout. Applicability and onboarding dates depend on taxpayer category and ETA decisions. This is an electronic reporting and validation framework; the precise document and transaction rules should be verified against current ETA specifications.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods may qualify for the 0% VAT rate when the statutory export conditions are met and export outside Egypt is evidenced. Exported services may qualify where the recipient is outside Egypt and the service satisfies the statutory conditions for export, including applicable recipient, use, and consumption requirements. Services supplied to or used or consumed in Egypt do not become zero-rated merely because the customer or payment intermediary is foreign. A streaming subscription supplied to viewers in Egypt is generally a domestic taxable supply unless a specific statutory rule applies. Input VAT recovery or refund remains subject to statutory eligibility, documentation, and ETA verification.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration and evidence of customs release/export
Bill of lading, airway bill, or other transport and delivery evidence for exported goods
Commercial invoice, export contract, and evidence identifying the foreign recipient

Bank records or other evidence of consideration and foreign-currency receipt where relevant; an inward remittance certificate is supporting evidence where available, not a universal statutory document for every export
For exported services: contract, service-delivery records, recipient and residence evidence, invoices, and evidence supporting the place of use or consumption and payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline applies to every Egyptian export transaction; sector-specific, contractual, banking, or other regulatory requirements may apply. ETA may deny zero-rating or input-tax recovery, assess underpaid VAT, and impose statutory late-payment additions and penalties where export conditions or evidence are insufficient. Fraudulent evasion may trigger the sanctions, including criminal consequences, prescribed by the VAT Law and other applicable laws. Assessment periods, penalties, and any criminal exposure depend on the conduct and current statutory provisions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — Al-Bank Al-Markazi Al-Masri (البنك المركزي المصري); the Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) exercises adjunct oversight of non-bank financial and capital-market activities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a unified, managed-floating exchange-rate regime as of March 2024, anchored by the CBE's FX liberalization under the IMF Extended Fund Facility. The Egyptian Pound (EGP) is internally convertible: all current-account transactions (goods, services, income, royalties) are bankable against underlying documentation and CBE purpose codes, with service remittances cleared within approximately 48 hours and dividend remittances within 5-7 business days post-reform. Capital-account transactions (foreign equity injection, shareholder loans, dividend and branch-profit repatriation) are legal and convertible but documentary-gated: they require audited financial statements, tax-clearance certificates, and bank FX-committee approval, and may be queued during episodic FX-scarcity periods. The EGP is non-convertible offshore — no deliverable EGP market exists outside Egypt — so all inward remittances must transit CBE-licensed authorized dealers. Profit-repatriation hurdles are materially reduced by completing the CBE Foreign-Capital Registration procedure, which legally guarantees transferability of registered capital and accrued profits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the CBE's consolidated foreign-exchange regulations (August 2024 circular amending the 2020 unified FX rules): (i) 100% of export proceeds — including digital-content and licensing receipts of the micro-drama business — must be repatriated to an account at an Egyptian authorized bank within the statutory timeline; (ii) for merchandise exports, proceeds must be received within 30 days of the bill-of-lading date for sight shipments, extending to a maximum of 120 days for usance/letter-of-credit terms; (iii) for services and digital exports, remittance must occur within 90 days of the invoice date or the contractual service-completion certificate; (iv) no mandatory conversion ratio to EGP is currently imposed — the 2016 float abolished forced surrender, so exporters may hold 100% of proceeds in foreign currency, converting only as needed to discharge EGP tax and operating liabilities; (v) late repatriation triggers CBE fines, exclusion from preferential FX facilities, and customs-liability consequences; and (vi) funds received by the bank must be posted to the exporter's FX account within 7 business days after nostro crediting.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Qatar National Bank Al Ahli (QNB Al Ahli)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account — EGP/USD, with UAE-corridor enhancement

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW as a primary collection or treasury rail, MEDIUM as a supplementary payout processor. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, DLocal, Stripe Treasury) are not authorized dealers under CBE Law 194/2020 and may not hold EGP or maintain virtual USD accounts intercepting Egyptian export receipts. Using them for primary revenue collection would breach the 100% repatriation mandate, expose the LLC to FX-control penalties, and risk account termination. A compliant hybrid model: collect subscription revenues through Apple IAP / Google Play / Stripe into the onshore operational account via platform-payout SWIFT MT103, and use an offshore EMI-vaulted debit/spend rail only for sub-USD 10,000 disbursements to international creators — never for converting EGP or maintaining onshore EGP balances.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person appearance is effectively mandatory for the initial corporate KYC interview at CIB, NBE, and Banque Misr. At least one natural-person signatory — the General Manager or a board director — must attend physically in Cairo with original passports and company book. Fully remote opening is not offered to newly incorporated foreign-owned LLCs; foreign directors may appoint a resident Egyptian signatory under a notarized and apostilled power of attorney, in which case the resident signatory appears in person while the foreign director is verified through a CBE-compliant video-e-KYC session supplemented by apostilled passport and address-proof documents. All signatories must pass CBE blacklist, UN/EU/OFAC sanctions, and PEP screening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly formed LLC with 100% non-resident (UAE or PRC) ownership, no audited operating history, and material projected digital revenue
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified UBO declaration up to the ultimate natural persons; apostilled certificates of incorporation and commercial-registry extracts for every shareholder layer; founders' source-of-wealth bank statements; accountant-reviewed 24-month cash-flow projections; executed subscriber monetization contracts and app-store listing evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Subscription receipts flowing via Apple IAP / Google Play / Stripe flagged as pass-through merchant activity or unregistered money-service business
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform distribution and merchant agreements; payout settlement reports evidencing platform-fee deduction (30%); subscriber-level transaction logs and VOID/refund reports; app-store financial-report dashboards; an internal compliance memo confirming the LLC acts only as a content-licensing merchant, never as an MSB/PSP.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Extreme transaction granularity: million-scale sub-USD 10 digital micro-payments inconsistent with classic trade-flow patterns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Revenue-analytics data-mart with daily transaction volume, average revenue per paying user, and conversion funnels; reconciliation of payout statements to the accounting GL; live public listings on Apple App Store and Google Play; a bank-accessible read-only dashboard to verify the operating model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border disbursements to dozens of semi-formal content creators, production agencies, and sub-licensees spanning Egypt, the UAE, and MENA/Asia jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed talent, production-service, and sublicense agreements; per-beneficiary payout register with invoices and signed receipts; Egyptian withholding-tax certificates for domestic creators (e.g., Form 41 filings); sanctions and PEP screening reports for each beneficiary; contract clauses indemnifying the bank against misuse; documented adherence to Egypt AML Law 80/2002 and CBE KYC thresholds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ambiguous media-licensing status of vertical short-drama production raising reputational or regulatory doubts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate architecture memo clarifying that the LLC produces and sublicenses content B2B while the independent streaming-app operator holds platform-side rights; SCMR content-compliance self-declaration and IP-assignment ledger; ISIC 5911 / NAICS 512110 mapping; confirmation that no statutory media license is required for the LLC's B2B production model and that the banking AML risk tier remains Low_Risk_Standard.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign shareholders inject equity via SWIFT MT103/MT202 wires to the LLC's capital escrow sub-account at an approved onshore bank (NBE / Banque Misr / CIB). The CBE Balance-of-Payments purpose code is 'Direct Investment in Egypt — Equity Capital'; the bank requires the certified articles of association, current commercial-registry extract, shareholder resolution, passport/UBO documentation, and a capital-registration application before crediting. Following credit confirmation, the bank issues the Foreign Capital Registration Certificate (Qaid Rasm al-Mal), which protects dividend and capital repatriation rights under the 2024 unified FX regime. Shareholders may retain funds in USD, convert to EGP at interbank rates, or hold a dual-currency position. Apple IAP / Google Play / Stripe payouts are commercial revenue and must NOT be wired to the escrow account; they flow into the operational USD account under service-export purpose codes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border service payments — creator payouts, production fees, software/platform subscriptions, advertising spend — each supported by the underlying contract and a CBE purpose code ('Payments for Services' or 'Royalties and License Fees'); royalty and technical-fee payments must evidence the 20% statutory Egyptian withholding tax (or treaty-reduced rate) remitted to the Egyptian Tax Authority, with a tax-clearance certificate retained; (ii) Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit (at-sight or usance up to 180 days) and documentary collections for physical merchandise tie-ins; (iii) SWIFT MT103 for dividend repatriation, requiring audited financial statements, a valid tax-clearance certificate, and bank FX-committee sign-off. Individual creator disbursements below USD 100,000 are executed through corporate internet-banking batch templates, while larger tickets escalate to the branch FX committee. Local EGP liquidity clears via the CBE RTGS system (STELLA) in near real time, and cross-currency conversion is executed at the interbank rate plus the applicable margin.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/EGP FX forwards (tenors up to 12 months) available at CIB, NBE, Banque Misr, and HSBC Egypt under CBE hedging regulations, requiring underlying trade or investment exposure documentation.
USD/EGP FX swaps and rollover swaps for intra-month liquidity and repatriation smoothing, subject to bank dealing-room credit lines.
Plain-vanilla purchased FX options (USD calls / EGP puts and USD puts / EGP calls) with domestic licensed banks, limited to hedging — speculative short-option writing is prohibited.

Cross-currency USD/EGP interest-rate swaps, permissible only with CBE pre-approval and solely against an underlying real foreign-currency liability; practical availability is limited for SME-scale treasuries.
Offshore EGP non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are prohibited for Egyptian-resident counterparties; no onshore NDF market exists — hedges must be executed deliverable onshore.
Natural revenue hedging via mandatory retention of USD subscription proceeds in an operational USD account and laddered forward conversion to EGP for projected tax and operating expenses.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registration Renewal (Company File Renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Commercial Registry One-Stop Shop
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based: renewal must be completed within 30 days after each anniversary of the initial commercial registration; for calendar-year LLCs, typically due before 31 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers escalating GAFI administrative fines (starting at approximately EGP 600 / USD 12) and temporary suspension of the commercial file; continued non-renewal results in administrative strike-off of the LLC from the Commercial Registry pursuant to the Companies Law No. 4 of 2022.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Declaration (CIT Return - Form No. 32) with Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal-year based: filing due within 4 months after the end of the tax year; for calendar-year LLCs the deadline is 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a fixed penalty of EGP 5,000 to 20,000 (approx. USD 100 to 400); unpaid tax accrues a 2% monthly late-payment addition under Article 137 of Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005. Persistent non-filing enables ETA bank-account garnishment, asset seizure, and criminal prosecution for tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Confirmation Declaration and Company File Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI / Commercial Registry, with AML supervision by the Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation due concurrently with the commercial-registration renewal and also no later than 30 days after any quotaholder transfer that changes the UBO structure.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omitting or misdeclaring UBO information draws penalties under the AML Law No. 80 of 2002 of up to EGP 500,000 (approx. USD 10,000), plus suspension of the GAFI file and prevention of share-transfer registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory without size or revenue threshold: every Egyptian LLC must appoint a licensed auditor registered with the Egyptian Central Auditors Authority to audit and certify the annual financial statements for quotaholder approval under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended by Law No. 4 of 2022.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), converged with IFRS; the audited financial statements must be prepared in Egyptian pounds and Arabic, and the balance sheet must be available for inspection by GAFI upon statutory request.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must keep a current Beneficial Ownership Register at the registered office and synchronize it with GAFI on each annual commercial-registration renewal. Any quotaholder transfer of 25% or more of the capital requires immediate amendment of the UBO register and submission of a fresh confirmation statement to the Commercial Registry within 30 days of the transfer, identifying all direct and indirect beneficial owners.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Quotaholders) and their capital contributions
Register of Directors/Managers and their powers
Minute Book of General Assembly and Management resolutions
Register of Auditors and annual audit reports

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - USD 900 per year (Egyptian registered-office agreement plus corporate secretarial and compliance agent service in Cairo)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 800 - USD 2,500 per year (certified audit of EAS-compliant financial statements with preparation of the CIT filing package)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% final corporate income tax rate on taxable profits of resident juridical persons (Law No. 91 of 2005 as amended, rates in force for FY 2024/2025).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No blanket tax holiday. Investment Law No. 72 of 2017: 50% tax deduction of invested capital over 5 years for strategic/labor-intensive projects approved by the competent committee, and 30% deduction for other qualifying projects. Law No. 206 of 2023 (Unified Tax Procedures Law) introduces a simplified presumptive regime for SMEs with annual turnover up to EGP 10 million, with tax computed at approximately 0.4%-1.5% of gross receipts (activity-dependent) and cash-basis accounting. Special economic zone regimes (e.g., Suez Canal Economic Zone) may provide up to 50% reduction for licensed zone entities. The micro-drama production LLC remains subject to the standard 22.5% regime unless it opts into the SME simplified regime.
